A walrus eats a clam without opening it.

The Boat.
In September twenty nineteen, a walrus attacked a Russian Navy landing boat and sank it.

The Haulout.
In September twenty fourteen, about thirty-five thousand walruses came ashore on one stretch of beach near Point Lay, Alaska.
They were spotted by the federal government's yearly aerial survey of Arctic marine mammals,
and four days earlier the same survey had seen only about fifteen hundred.
At the twenty twenty census, Point Lay had three hundred and thirty people,
which works out at about a hundred walruses for every person in town.
Walruses are bottom feeders in shallow water,

Federal wildlife officials list trampling at disturbed haulouts among the largest known natural causes of death for walruses,
